examples.text: Our duty is urged, and our confidence abetted.

The elements, however, abetted me in making a path through the deepest snow in the woods, for when I had once gone through the wind blew the oak leaves into my tracks, where they lodged, and by absorbing the rays of the sun melted the snow, and so not only made a dry bed for my feet, but in the night their dark line was my guide.

glosses: To urge on, stimulate (a person to do) something desirable.
To back up one's forecast of a doubtful issue, by staking money, etc., to bet.
Fraud or cunning.
An act of abetting; of helping; of giving aid.
To disturb or excite; to perturb or stir up (a person).

examples.text: He was greatly agitated by the news.

glosses: To cause to move with a violent, irregular action; to shake.

examples.text: to agitate water in a vessel
The wind agitates the sea.

glosses: To participate in political agitation (sense 3).

examples.text: NAMBLA is working to build a coalition of gay, lesbian, progressive and civil liberties groups to agitate against the increasing state attacks on gay men who associate with boys.

glosses: To set in motion; to actuate.

examples.text: Your speech at the time a bill for the regency was agitated now lies before me.

glosses: To mull over, or think deeply about; to consider, to devise.

examples.text: Politicians agitate desperate designs.

glosses: To stir up or excite; to rouse or goad into action.
